question: You deposit €1,000 in an account that pays 10% a year. At the end of each year the bank adds the interest to the account, and you withdraw nothing. Predict (1) how many euros of interest the bank adds at the end of year 3 and (2) the balance after 3 years. Give two numbers and justify them in one or two sentences.
answer:
(a) 100
(b) 1300
(c) Same 10% every year so 100 each year.
feedback: 10% of 1,000 is 100. Your answer keeps the base at €1,000.

to_work_on.what: what the 10% is charged on each year

question: €400 at 5% a year, interest added each year. How many euros of interest are added in year 2? (a number)

You deposit €2,000 in an account that pays 5% a year; the interest is added at the end of each year and you withdraw nothing. Predict (1) the interest added at the end of year 3 and (2) the balance after 3 years, and justify them. Then explain why the year 3 interest is not €100, and say what would happen to the yearly interest if you withdrew each year's interest as soon as it was added. Answer with two numbers and two or three sentences.
answer:
(a) 110.25
(b) 2315.25
(c) 5% on a balance that already holds 205 of interest; withdrawn it stays 100.
feedback: Both numbers are right. You have it.
